title.narrative: Enhancing Collection of Revenue and Expenditure Management Project

description.narrative: The ENCORE remains a well-performing project supporting difficult governance reforms that are critical to the national development priorities of DRC. The proposed Additional Financing will scale up activities to buttress expenditure management reforms implemented under ENCORE and include deepened support for independent oversight arrangements at central level. The AF will also expand support for improved resource management to three additional provinces (Kongo Central, Equateur, and Maniema).
The project development objective is to increase mining revenue transparency and improve expenditure management at the central level and in the project provinces

title.narrative: Percentage increase in Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) collected by project provinces

comment.narrative: At the end of September 2025, the cumulative periodic trend of revenues collected by the provincial tax administrations (excluding Kasai) reveals their increase of 20.3% (CDF 12,996,625,067.52 against CDF 10,806,114,021.76). The management of the taxpayer register has been improved through the census and the registration of taxpayers in electronic files. Thus, 178,627 taxpayers have been recorded in the provinces capitals and some territories of the provinces ENCORE.

title.narrative: Transparent mechanism for mining revenue transfer to local communities adopted and effective

baseline.value: FFG Decree is not consistent with FFG objectives and activities and inter-ministerial Decree for 0.3% sharing is not available

target.value: FFG's Revised Decree is satisfactorily implemented and Inter-ministerial Decree for 0.3% sharing is satisfactorily implemented

comment.narrative: In June 2025, the Court of Auditors published the results of its audit of the management of the allocation of 0.3% of turnover by specialized entities (DOTS). The audit revealed a poor distribution of revenues, a lack of accounting in accordance with OHADA law, the non-existence of project execution units, as well as a widespread violation of public procurement procedures. The audit also highlighted abusive practices of mining companies, including the refusal to communicate their turnover, the withholding of endowments due and fraudulent reductions. These findings of the Court of Auditors' audits were confirmed by the BSA report produced in August 2025 with ENCORE. Also, in September 2025, AfreWhash published its audit report which emphasizes the low rate of DOT implementation. Out of nearly 102 companies in the production phase, 46 were established and about sixty remain.

actual.value: The Decree for 0.3% sharing was approved in december 2021 and decree modifying FOMIN was approved in February 2023, and they are being satisfactorily implemented.

title.narrative: DRC progress in meeting 3 specific EITI requirements from the 2019 EITI Scorecard (State Participation (requirement #2.6); Direct Subnational payments (#4.6); and Subnational transfers (#5.2))

baseline.value: DRC is making “meaningful progress” to meet these 3 requirements under 2016 EITI Standard (DRC EITI Report Oct 2019)

target.value: DRC fully meets all of the 3 requirements under 2019 EITI Standard (i.e. DRC scores 90 points for the 3 requirements meaning “ The broader objective of the requirement has been fulfilled, and all required aspects of the requirement have been addressed" )

comment.narrative: Activities to strengthen the process of elaboration, validation, publication and dissemination of the EITI-DRC technical secretariat's reports have carried out : (i) launching, data collection, improvement and validation of the 2023 scoping report; (ii) recruitment of the ENERTEAM firm which will support the EITI-DRC Secretariat in the process of preparing the 2023 annual report according to EITI standards; (iii) launching awareness and collecting data from public administrations and entities, as well as from all identified mining companies. The draft of the 2023 EITI annual report has been prepared and will be published by 31 December 2025 at the latest. This report will not only allow the DRC to meet the corrective measures and recommendations arising from the last validation as well as previous EITI Reports, but also and above all to improve its score at the next evaluation which will start on 1 January 2026, and which will be done in accordance with the 2023 EITI Standard.

actual.value: The draft of the 2023 DRC EITI Report 2023 has been prepared and will be published in December.

title.narrative: Number of Accounting Department Units (DGTCP) operational in provinces

comment.narrative: A commission has been set up in the Cabinet of the Minister of Finance to identify the civil servants of the provincial divisions of the Ministry of Finance who will be selected to work in accounting positions in the provinces.

title.narrative: Selected strategic SOEs publishing annual financial audit reports

comment.narrative: The Superior Council of the Portfolio has published on its recently updated website with the support of ENCORE the financial statements of SOEs for 2023 and 2024 respectively for 10 (GECAMINES, MIBA, SNCC, RVA, SONAS, CVM, LMC, ONATRA, SODIMICO, SONAHYDROC) in March and June 2025 and 4 (SOKIMO, SONAS, LMC, and SNCC) in October 2025. Six of these SOEs are among nine SOEs targeted by ENCORE to increase transparency.

title.narrative: Number of Line Ministries trusted with budget commitment authority (PBC #1)

baseline.value: Budget commitment authority is concentrated at the Ministry of Finance level. No Line Ministry is granted with the budget commitment authority.

target.value: PBC#1.5: Budget commitment authority transferred to eight (8) Line Ministries.

comment.narrative: To link the IT system of the Central Bank of Congo to Gesdepenses, in the four pilot ministries (Health, Primary education, Rural development, Infrastructures and public works) for the deconcentration of budget commitment authority in the first quarter of 2026, an interfacing IT application (IBM software) has been acquired. This IBM software will allow the expenditure chain to be in line with the migration of the Central Bank of Congo's payment system recently carried out. As for the deployment of accounting positions, on August 28, 2025, accountants and administrative staff were appointed for the 6 accounting positions to serve the 9 pilot ministries. The deeds opening the operating accounts for the six accountants have been signed.

actual.value: In the first quarter of 2026, budget commitment authority will be transferred to 9 line ministries.

title.narrative: Annual Budget Review Reports approved and published for Central Government and for selected provinces

baseline.value: Central Government 2019 annual budget review report published on July 2021

target.value: Central Government 2025 annual budget review report published by end of September 2026

comment.narrative: The Court of Auditors produced the 2024 budget execution report of Central Government in November 2025. This report was presented to Parliament, but it has not yet been published on its website. Regarding the provinces, the Court of Auditors received the 2024 budget execution reports of Kasaï, Kasaï Central, Kasaï Oriental, and Lomami. These were reviewed and transmitted for adoption to the joint chambers (in August 2025 for Kasaï and Lomami, in October for Kasaï Oriental, and in November 2025 for Kasaï Central).

actual.value: In November 2025, the CoA produced the 2024 budget execution report of the Central Government.

title.narrative: TSA established and rolled-out in central government

baseline.value: Central government funds are dispersed across multiple, sometimes unauthorized, bank accounts managed by officials

target.value: The TSA Action Plan is implemented satisfactorily to the Bank

comment.narrative: The stress test of the impact of closing bank accounts in commercial banks on the financial system was carried out in October 2025, based on a database of 3,700 accounts identified by the Central Bank of Congo (BCC). A strategy for closing bank accounts is being prepared and will be adopted by the Government. A database of 11,276 bank accounts inventoried by COREF in 2023 was shared with the BCC

actual.value: A strategy for closing bank accounts was prepared after carrying out the stress test of its impact on the financial system in October 2025.

title.narrative: An audited, clean, and complete database of civil servants is available for central government (PBC#2)

baseline.value: Current central government staff database is incomplete and is reported to include irregularities, discrepancies, and thousands of ghost workers

target.value: PBC#2.5: A clean and complete integration of the different civil servants databases is available and automatically linked/integrated to the Recipient's payroll system.

comment.narrative: The process of cleaning up FRAP database was carried out in 22 provinces, with the validation and identification of 354,305 civil servants out of the 1,264,748 declared. The recruitment of the IVA for the achievement of PBC#2.1 to PBC#2.4 is underway, the contract is expected to be signed in the second half of March 2026. Regarding the Human Resources Management and Information System (HRMIS), a report on the optimization of HR and payroll management macro-processes was produced by a consultant in September 2025. This report aims to standardize procedures across government entities, rationalize and optimize workflows to reduce irregularities, and establish a technical foundation for HRMIS configuration. It covers the full lifecycle of civil service management through seven macro-processes: budget forecasting for remuneration, recruitment, administrative management, career management, training/skills administration, payroll execution, and cessation of activity.

actual.value: The civil servants' database has been cleaned up in 22 provinces.

title.narrative: Number of central line ministries using IFMIS platform

baseline.value: IFMIS is not available. The government uses an outdated and ineffective budget execution system

target.value: IFMIS platform is deployed at least in two additional central line ministries

comment.narrative: The consortium KPMG RDC and KPMG Tunisia was recruited in June 2025 to provide project management assistance for IFMIS, with the core consisting of the budgetary, accounting, and treasury management modules (preliminary studies and analysis of additional needs in capacity building and equipment). The results of this assistance will make it possible to prepare the terms of reference for launching the recruitment process of the firm that will implement the IFMIS.

actual.value: The consortium KPMG RDC and KPMG Tunisia recruited in June 2025 is assisting the Government to prepare the terms of reference for launching the recruitment process of the firm that will implement the IFMIS.

title.narrative: Percent of fiscal transfers available to Recipient's provinces (PBC#4)

baseline.value: No formal mechanism is available for distributing national revenue (40%) between provinces

target.value: PBC#4.5: Based on the ArrêtE(s), the Recipient has released annually to all Recipient's provinces an amount equivalent to a percentage of the 40% of the total national revenue calculated based on the formula established in the ArrêtEs, as set forth in the PBC Manual, in a subsequent year.

comment.narrative: The report of the IVA (COFIMA firm) was partially approved, and 80% (US$14,921,389.84) of eligible expenditures were reimbursed in June 2025. The additional audit report on the sample of 348 agents was produced and shared with the World Bank for the disbursement of 20 percent of the remaining amount. The recruitment process for the completion of PBC#4 IVA (targets 4.4 and 4.5) is underway, and the contract is expected to be signed in early January 2026.

actual.value: The report of the IVA (COFIMA) for achievement of PBC#4.3 was partially approved, and 80% (US$14,921,389.84) of eligible expenditures were reimbursed in June 2025. The recruitment process of the IVA for PBC#4.4 and PBC#4.5 is ongoing with an expected signing date of January 2026.

title.narrative: Up-to-date database on household living conditions at national level available

baseline.value: No recent data since the latest national household survey including consumption data was implemented in 2012

target.value: Database on Household Poverty for the recent years available

comment.narrative: This indicator tracks the implementation of household survey activities from data collection to the production and dissemination of survey results and reports. The Poverty Survey Report has been prepared and submitted for independent review. The final draft of the report has been produced and is expected to be published at the end of December 2025.

actual.value: The final draft of the report has been produced and is expected to be published at the end of December 2025.

title.narrative: Satisfactory digital solutions for revenue collection and management established in project provinces

baseline.value: None of the project provinces avail digital solutions for revenue collection which are fully operational and satisfactory

target.value: Satisfactorily digital solutions are available in all four project provinces

comment.narrative: The consultant who will prepare the technical specifications of digital solutions for revenue collection is in the negotiation phase of the contract. It is expected that his contract will be signed on December 15 and will be able to start work in early 2026.

actual.value: No digital solutions for revenue collection and management have yet been developed.

title.narrative: Consolidated, relevant, and comprehensive budget reports and financial statements in project provinces are produced and available

baseline.value: Quarterly budget reports are prepared and published in none of the project provinces. No Annual Financial reports meeting accounting standards is currently prepared

target.value: Quarterly budget reports are prepared and regularly published on all four project provinces websites and financial reports meeting new accounting standards are produced by existing DGTCP provincial units, then submitted to CoA

comment.narrative: The four ENCORE provinces have drawn up their edicts on the accounts of the 2024 budget statement.

actual.value: The four ENCORE provinces have drawn up their edicts on the accounts of the 2024 budget statement.

title.narrative: Share of line ministries using e-procurement system (PBC#3)

baseline.value: SIGMAP, a system already developed by the government, is ready to be rolled out.

target.value: PBC#3.5: The E-procurement system is operational in one (1) additional Line Ministry.

comment.narrative: The roadmap for the operationalization of SIGMAP has been delayed despite the completion of all the legal prerequisites. The renewal of equipment in the 20 pilot procurement units, the equipment of the SIGMAP room at the Ministry of Budget, and the training of additional users within the pilot procurement units are among the prerequisites for the rolling out of SIGMAP. The firm that will develop, configure and deploy e-GP has been recruited. The following deliverables were produced by this firm: (i) launch deliverables (project plan, quality assurance plan, service agreement, and scoping note), and (ii) general design deliverables (general functional specification files, ergonomic and performance requirements, and mock-up).

actual.value: The firm that will develop, configure and deploy the e-procurement system (e-GP) has been recruited.

title.narrative: Number of Accounting Department Units (DGTCP) operational in central ministries

baseline.value: The national Accounting Department (DGTCP) is not yet formally established

target.value: Accounting Department (DGTCP) Unit is established in one additional line ministry

comment.narrative: Seven accounting positions have been created (six for the 9 ministries for the deconcentration of budget commitment authority and the Central Accounting Agency of the Treasury) and all the public accounts and administrative personnel have been recruited and appointed. The network of public accountants is expected to be operational by January 2026.

actual.value: Zero accounting units at DGTCP are operational. Seven accountings units have been created and staffed, which will be operational in the first quarter of 2026.
